stem:
Qasim fills a plastic syringe with air and seals the tip with his finger. When he pushes the plunger in, the air is squeezed into a smaller volume.

Why can the air be compressed?

options.text: There are large spaces between the air particles, so they can be forced closer together.
The air particles themselves shrink when the plunger is pushed.
The air particles change into liquid particles when pushed together.
The air particles escape through the walls of the syringe.

teacher.key_rationale: Gas can be compressed because large spaces separate its particles; pushing the plunger forces those particles closer and decreases volume. Particles do not shrink, liquefy, or escape through sealed walls.
